no, taking the bishop on e6 doesn't get the king out of check. your knight on d7 is giving check from d7, not from e6, so the king has to answer that check first and can't grab the bishop this turn. after it moves, your knight still forks the king's escape and the bishop on f8.

yes, actually - i read that wrong. king to e6 does escape check, because your knight on d7 doesn't attack e6, only f6, f8, b8, b6, c5, e5. so mallow can take your bishop there.

but that's fine: your knight on d7 then attacks the bishop on f8. you take it right back with knight takes f8, so the bishops trade evenly and your knight lands active near mallow's king.

you're right, and that's exactly what the fact list shows: knight to d7+ moved away, but your bishop on e6 was left with nothing guarding it, so mallow's king got out of check by capturing it. that move never protected the bishop, it just forced the king to choose, and it chose your bishop.

the upside is still there though: your knight now sits on d7 hitting her bishop on f8, which nothing defends. play knight takes on f8, check, and you get the bishop back.
